items.prompt: What's the key test this unit uses to distinguish being tired from being burned out?
choices: How many hours of sleep someone got the previous night

Whether rest actually resolves it — ordinary tiredness recovers with genuine rest and the person's relationship to the work returns to normal; burnout's cynicism and reduced-efficacy components largely persist even after real, adequate rest
How long someone has been at their current job
Whether the person complains about being tired out loud
items.explanation: The distinguishing test isn't severity, it's whether rest resolves the state. Burnout specifically includes components (cynicism, reduced efficacy) that aren't about depleted energy, so rest alone — which directly addresses only exhaustion — doesn't fully resolve them.

items.prompt: Per L1/L2, does exhaustion alone (with no cynicism or reduced efficacy) constitute burnout in the fuller sense this unit describes?
choices: Yes — exhaustion alone is sufficient to define burnout

No — burnout specifically requires cynicism/depersonalization and reduced efficacy alongside exhaustion; exhaustion alone is a strong signal of ordinary overwork or poor sleep, not the fuller burnout pattern
No, because burnout doesn't include exhaustion as a component at all
Yes, but only if the exhaustion has lasted more than a year
items.explanation: The three-component model requires all three (or at least exhaustion plus one of the other two, per the loosely-converged research this unit summarizes) — exhaustion in isolation is exactly the kind of sign that's genuinely ambiguous between ordinary tiredness and something more serious, which is why the other two components matter for distinguishing them.

items.prompt: Per L2, why is burnout specifically hard to self-diagnose compared to many other health-adjacent issues?
choices: Because burnout has no observable symptoms at all

Because the cynicism component doesn't just color feelings about work — it also colors how seriously someone takes their own early warning signs ("am I just being dramatic"), so the condition actively undermines its own detection
Because burnout only affects people who don't pay attention to their own wellbeing
Because burnout is purely a physical condition with no psychological component
items.explanation: This is the self-referential trap L2 describes explicitly: cynical self-doubt about whether the signs are 'real enough' is itself part of the same pattern, which is why checking against a specific, named list is more reliable than trusting a general instinct that's compromised by the condition it's meant to detect.

items.prompt: How does this unit connect to the negative-returns curve from `sustainable-performance/myth-linear-output`?
choices: It doesn't — the two units cover unrelated topics

Burnout is presented as a plausible real mechanism behind that curve at a longer time horizon: exhaustion raises error rate, cynicism degrades care in catching errors, and reduced efficacy removes motivation to course-correct — three compounding contributors to declining net output over months
Burnout is presented as the ONLY possible cause of the negative-returns curve, with no other contributing factors
The connection is that burnout only happens to people who already work past 60 hours a week
items.explanation: L2 explicitly ties the three burnout components to the mechanism described in the earlier unit — not as the sole explanation, but as a real, plausible longer-timescale contributor to the same shape (net output declining despite, or because of, continued effort).

items.prompt: In L3, both engineers experienced identical early signs at the same times. What actually caused Path A to take four months longer to surface as a visible problem than Path B?
choices: Path A's engineer was working on a harder project than Path B's

Path A dismissed each sign individually (as sprint pressure, normal venting, ordinary tiredness) rather than checking it against the specific three-component list, falling into the self-referential trap; Path B explicitly named the combination of components early, which made the signal harder to dismiss and enabled an earlier, targeted response
Path B's engineer had a fundamentally different personality that made them immune to burnout
Path A's team was less supportive than Path B's team from the very start
items.explanation: L3 is explicit that both engineers had identical initial signs — the difference was entirely in recognition, driven by whether the signs were checked against the specific component list or individually rationalized away, which is exactly the self-referential trap and its antidote from L2.

items.prompt: Per L3's third failure mode, why didn't Path A's genuine, fully-disconnected week off resolve the underlying problem?
choices: Because the vacation wasn't long enough — a longer vacation would have fully resolved it

Because rest directly addresses exhaustion but not cynicism or reduced efficacy — treating rest as a universal fix regardless of which components are actually present leaves the non-exhaustion components (and their actual driver, unsustainable load) unaddressed
Because vacations have no physiological effect on burnout whatsoever
Because Path A's engineer didn't genuinely disconnect during the vacation
items.explanation: L3 explicitly frames this as a mismatch between the fix (rest, which addresses exhaustion) and the actual problem (all three components, driven by unsustainable load) — Path B's eventual recovery came from addressing the load directly, not from rest alone, which is exactly what Path A's experience already demonstrated wouldn't be sufficient.
